items.title: US sinks Iranian warship as strikes expand inland

featured_image.name: US strikes Iranian warship near Sri Lanka, over 100 missing

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine returned to the Pentagon podium Wednesday for their second briefing since Operation Epic Fury began, as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran entered its fifth day with no signs of abating. According to Reuters, officials said Iran is firing fewer missiles than at the outset of the conflict and that U.S. strikes would expand deeper into Iranian territory.[1]

The briefing came as the U.S. military disclosed it had struck an Iranian warship off the coast of Sri Lanka in the Indian Ocean, according to a Reuters exclusive citing three U.S. officials. The IRIS Dena, a 180-crew frigate, sank after what Sri Lankan defense sources described as a submarine attack, leaving at least 101 crew members missing and one confirmed dead. Sri Lanka's navy launched a rescue operation after receiving a distress call off the southern coast near Galle, with Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath telling parliament that at least 30 survivors had been pulled from the water. If confirmed as a submarine kill, it would mark the first time a submersible has sunk a warship in combat in decades.[2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: U.S. stocks rise after report Iran contacted CIA to discuss ending war

featured_image.name: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq rise on Iran war hopes, upbeat jobs data

items.description: The escalating war between the United States, Israel, and Iran sent shockwaves through global financial markets and supply chains this week, halting shipping through one of the world's most critical trade corridors and driving oil prices sharply higher. The crisis, now in its fifth day, has rattled investors, grounded thousands of flights, and raised the specter of a sustained inflation shock.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rise as oil steadies on fifth day of Iran conflict

featured_image.name: Oil surges for second day, Brent tops $83 after Iran orders Strait of Hormuz closure

items.description:
U.S. stock futures turned positive early Wednesday as oil prices steadied, offering a reprieve from days of turbulence triggered by the U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran that began Saturday, February 28. The S&P 500 futures pointed to gains at the open, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite futures also climbed, according to The Wall Street Journal, which reported that both futures and oil prices were stabilizing as the conflict entered its fifth day.[1]

The tentative calm followed a pivotal move by President Donald Trump on Tuesday, who announced the U.S. would offer political risk insurance through the Development Finance Corporation and deploy the Navy to escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz "if necessary," according to Bloomberg. "Regardless of circumstances, the United States will guarantee the UNINTERRUPTED FLOW of ENERGY to the WORLD," Trump wrote on Truth Social. The announcement helped cap a sharp rally in crude prices, with Brent briefly topping $85 per barrel before settling lower on Tuesday.[2][3][4]

items.title: NATO destroys Iranian missile heading toward Turkey

featured_image.name: NATO defence systems intercept Iranian attack targeting Turkey

items.description:
NATO air and missile defense systems destroyed a ballistic missile fired from Iran toward Turkish airspace on Wednesday, Turkey's defense ministry announced, marking the first time a NATO member has been directly targeted in the six-day-old US-Israeli war against Iran. The missile, which traveled through Iraqi and Syrian airspace before being intercepted over the eastern Mediterranean, sent debris from the intercepting NATO missile falling into Turkey's southern Hatay province.[1][2][3]

The interception represents a dramatic shift in the conflict. Until Wednesday, Iran had deliberately avoided targeting Turkey despite the presence of US forces at multiple sensitive installations on Turkish soil, including the Incirlik air base near Adana and the Kurecik early-warning radar station.[4][5]

items.title: Greenland's fishermen face a crisis as warming Arctic melts the sea ice they depend on

featured_image.name: 'It's too warm': Greenland's fishermen are under threat from climate change

items.description:
Fisherman Helgi Áargil no longer knows what to expect on Greenland's fjords. Last year, his boat got stuck in ice that calved from a nearby glacier. This year, it has been unusually wet. His income swings between roughly 100,000 Danish kroner (about $15,700) per outing and nothing at all, according to reporting by the Associated Press from Ilulissat, Greenland.[1]

The Arctic is warming faster than any other region on the planet, and the consequences for Greenland's fishing-dependent economy are becoming harder to ignore. Fishing accounts for up to 95% of the territory's exports, with China, the United States, Japan, and Europe among the top markets.[2][1]

featured_image.name: Iran live news: Trump under fire from Democrats, Israel pounds Lebanon

items.description: Explosions rang out across Tehran and Jerusalem early Wednesday as the war between Iran, the United States, and Israel entered its fifth day with no sign of de-escalation. Dawn broke over the Iranian capital to the sound of blasts from fresh U.S.-Israeli airstrikes, while Israel's military said it activated air defense systems to intercept incoming Iranian missiles, with explosions heard around Jerusalem.[1][2]

items.title: Iran begins three-day farewell ceremony for Khamenei in Tehran

featured_image.name: Khamenei's death shakes Islamic Republic, Iran switches to ...

items.description:
Iran is holding a three-day public farewell ceremony for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader killed at age 86 in joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on February 28, with plans to bury him in the holy city of Mashhad, his birthplace.

The ceremony began late Wednesday at Tehran's Imam Khomeini Prayer Hall, according to Reuters, which reported that Hojjatoleslam Mahmoudi, head of Iran's Islamic Propagation Council, invited the public to pay their respects starting at 10 p.m. local time. Details of the funeral procession are to be announced separately. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on its Telegram account that a "large farewell ceremony" would be held in the capital before the burial.[1][2][3]

items.title: IDF says 300 Iranian missile launchers destroyed in 6 days of strikes

items.description: Six days into "Operation Epic Fury," US and Israeli forces have destroyed approximately 300 Iranian ballistic missile launchers and struck thousands of targets across the country, but Iran's network of underground missile facilities continues to pose a challenge for the combined air campaign.[1][2]

items.title: US, Israel hit 3,300 targets in Iran but underground missile sites resist airstrikes

featured_image.name: Israel's strikes on Iran spark interest in air-launched ...

items.description: As the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its fifth day, destroying Tehran's ballistic missile capabilities has emerged as a central — and elusive — objective. Since the coordinated strikes began on February 28, US and Israeli forces have hit over 3,300 targets across Iran, yet military analysts warn that much of Iran's missile arsenal remains sheltered deep underground in fortified "missile cities" that conventional airpower may be unable to reach.[1][2]

items.title: South Korea halts trading as Asian markets plunge on Iran war fears

featured_image.name: South Korea’s stock market in meltdown amid US-Iran war

items.description:
Asian stock markets suffered steep losses on Wednesday as the widening war between the United States, Israel, and Iran sent oil prices climbing higher and rattled investor confidence across the region. South Korea's Kospi plunged as much as 10%, triggering circuit breakers that temporarily halted trading, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 4% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 2.8%.[1]

The sell-off marks the deepest rout in Asian equities since the U.S. and Israel launched coordinated strikes on Iran late on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and sparking retaliatory attacks across the region. President Donald Trump has signaled the military campaign could last weeks.[2][3][4]

items.title: Study finds Northern Hemisphere losing snow cover three times faster than gaining it

featured_image.name: Study reveals a widespread decline of snow cover in the ...

items.description: Researchers at Mississippi State University have published a new study showing that snow cover across the Northern Hemisphere is declining, with nearly three times as many regions losing snow as gaining it. The findings, published in January in the Journal of Hydrometeorology, add to a growing body of evidence that warming temperatures are reshaping seasonal snow patterns across the globe.

items.title: US and Ecuador launch joint military strikes on drug cartels

featured_image.name: Ecuador calls off arms exchange with US over plan to send ...

items.description:
Ecuadorian and U.S. military forces launched joint operations against designated terrorist organizations inside Ecuador on March 3, marking a new front in the South American nation's escalating war against drug cartels. The U.S. Southern Command announced the operations, calling them "a powerful example of the commitment of partners in Latin America and the Caribbean to combat the scourge of" narco-terrorism.[1]

The launch follows a weekend of high-level meetings in Quito, where SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan met with President Daniel Noboa and senior defense officials on March 1-2 to finalize plans for security cooperation. Noboa announced the initiative on X, writing: "In March, we will carry out joint operations alongside our regional allies, including the United States".[2][3][4]

items.title: UN warns El Niño could return later this year

featured_image.name: El Niño is creating an unexpected atmospheric pattern, but ...

items.description:
The World Meteorological Organization warned on Tuesday that El Niño could develop later this year as the current La Niña weakens, a shift that climate scientists say could push global temperatures toward new records in 2027.

The WMO's latest update, issued March 3, forecasts a 60% chance of neutral conditions — neither El Niño nor La Niña — during March through May, rising to 70% during April through June. But the probability of El Niño increases steadily thereafter, reaching roughly 40% by May through July.[1][2]

items.description: A powerful iPhone hacking toolkit that appears to have originated in government surveillance operations has spread to foreign espionage groups and financially motivated cybercriminals, according to research published Tuesday by Google's Threat Intelligence Group and mobile security firm iVerify.

items.title: Carney says US-Israel strikes on Iran appear to violate international law

featured_image.name: Canada calls rising escalation in Middle East result of ...

items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called on Wednesday for the "rapid de-escalation" of the conflict triggered by joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, saying the war represented "another example of the failure of the international order". Speaking at a press conference in Sydney, Australia, during an official visit, Carney offered his sharpest critique yet of how the military operation has been conducted, even as he reaffirmed Canada's support for neutralizing Iran's nuclear threat.[1][2]

items.title: Ship hit near UAE's Fujairah as Gulf attacks escalate

featured_image.name: Three tankers damaged in Gulf and one seafarer killed as US ...

items.description: A commercial vessel was hit by an unknown projectile approximately 7 nautical miles east of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported on March 4. The ship's master reported that the projectile caused damage to the vessel's steel plating, though all crew members were safe with no fire or water ingress detected onboard, according to UKMTO.[1]
